propositions: When multiple findings across review passes share a single root cause (incomplete enumeration), the author receives N instance-level fixes without signal that the method itself is faulty, allowing the loop to persist across multiple passes.

A population-based coaching move scoped to criteria where a named instance is drawn from a larger set (G1G2, E4, G6, A1) must reframe the fix as complete enumeration plus a machine-checkable acceptance criterion that fails while any instance remains.

The new move 15 'sample, not the population' with template requiring population enumeration and verifiable completeness proof must be added to MOVE_REGISTRY as an addition-only change, mirrored in docs, and scoped via applies_when to prevent application to unrelated reviews.

Existing moves 12 and 10 and 13 demonstrate that additive scoped coaching moves are the pattern; move 15 belongs in the built-in registry rather than project overlay because its four triggers are core criteria.
The move registry, docs table, and applicability assertions must maintain bidirectional consistency enforced by existing tests, and no existing move attributes may be modified.
